blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A Batch job starts the lesson's solve worker with no RESULT_BUCKET, a 12-character SNAPSHOT_DIGEST and TIME_LIMIT_S set to "fast". What does the worker do?

options.text: It reports the first problem only, and exits with code 2 before it reads any snapshot
options.says: The page: 'All three mistakes are reported at once', in one refusal message.

options.text: It reports all three problems in one message, and exits with code 0 so Batch retries it
options.says: Exit code 0 means the job succeeded; the worker returns 2, and 'its exit code tells Batch the job failed'.

options.text: It reports all three problems in one message, and exits with code 2, reading no snapshot
options.says: Right: every problem is collected first, the refusal comes before any snapshot is read, and main returns 2.

options.text: It reports all three problems in one message, and writes a failed result for the run in S3
options.says: The page: the refusal comes before any snapshot is read or any solve starts, and no result is written.

origin.section: Settings Come From the Environment, All Checked Before the Solve

questions.stem: A CP-SAT roster worker runs as a Fargate job sized at 4 vCPUs, on a host with many more cores. Its job sets PYTHON_CPU_COUNT=4 and leaves num_workers at its default. What should change, by the lesson?

options.text: Nothing: CP-SAT reads PYTHON_CPU_COUNT through Python, so it starts 4 workers
options.says: The page: PYTHON_CPU_COUNT changes what Python's functions report, and CP-SAT counts cores in its C++ code, not through Python.

options.text: Set num_workers to 4: its default of 0 follows what the machine shows, not the 4 vCPUs
options.says: Right: num_workers 0 means trying to use all cores on the machine, and inside a container the machine may be the host, not the job's share.

options.text: Set num_workers to 4: its default of 0 runs a single worker, leaving three vCPUs idle
options.says: The parameter file says 0 means using all cores; 1 is the value that means no parallelism.

options.text: Set num_workers to 0: its default of 1 runs one search, leaving three vCPUs idle
options.says: The default is 0, not 1: the parameter file says 0 means trying to use all cores on the machine.

origin.section: Tell the Solver How Many CPUs the Container Has

questions.stem: A teammate proposes an ENV line in the Dockerfile with an AWS access key, so the solve worker can write its results to S3. What does the lesson say instead?

options.text: Keep the key in ENV: ENV values are encrypted in the image, so a private image keeps it safe
options.says: The page: anyone who can pull an image can read every file and every ENV in it.

options.text: Keep the key out of ENV and list it in .dockerignore, which hands it to the container only at run time
options.says: .dockerignore filters the build context so files never reach the image; it hands nothing to a running container.

options.text: Keep the key out of ENV and COPY a .env file holding it, as the files in an image stay unreadable
options.says: The page: anyone who can pull an image can read every file in it, so the image holds no AWS keys and no .env file; .dockerignore keeps .env out.

options.text: Keep the key out of the image, and give the Batch job a role that supplies credentials at run time
options.says: Right: the image holds no secret; the job role (jobRoleArn) gives the container temporary credentials boto3 finds itself.

origin.section: The Image Runs as a Non-Root User and Holds No Credentials
